set.approach: Park in one of the turnouts beside the road at Courtright Reservoir, just before Trapper Springs Campground, and walk to the granite slabs; there is no real trail. Skirt the base of the dome's south faces to the Lower Tier. The route is a left-leaning crack to slab, right of the black water streak that carries the bolted line to its left; gear low, bolts above.

review.notes: Area page for the approach; route page for the start position and any stated descent.

set.approach: Park in one of the turnouts beside the road at Courtright Reservoir, just before Trapper Springs Campground, and walk to the granite slabs; there is no real trail. Skirt the base of the dome's south faces to the Lower Tier. It is on the left margin of the huge shield, with Organ Grinder on one side and the direct start of Republicans on Crack on the other, climbing past bolts to a flake and on up the face.

set.approach: Pull off opposite Kidd Creek, cross the road, and take the worn track up the creek bed until boulder-hopping to the left bank becomes possible. From there a steep slope reaches the broad gully that serves The Underworld, and this buttress sits immediately right of that gully. The route is the slab just left of Toetally Broken.

review.notes: Area page for the approach; route page for the start position and any stated descent.

set.approach: Follow the High Sierra Trail to Tamarack Lake, where most parties camp; a day trip from Lone Pine Meadow is also possible. From the lake it is about an hour up to the Main Wall, a north-facing wall above the Lilliput Glacier. The route aims for the huge dihedral on the left flank of the tooth at mid-wall, reached by crack and ledge climbing into a left-facing corner.
set.descent_text: From the top-out, scramble fourth class west into the gap that separates the main wall from Dawn Pillar and rappel into it (slung block and a single-bolt anchor), then scramble out the far side and hike third class down to a prominent gully. Another rappel drops into the gully, and from there you scramble down; take gear to build or back up anchors. The main wall can also be descended by going over the summit and east then north to Lion Rock Pass (class 2) and back to the lake.

review.notes: Route page for the west descent and the dihedral; area pages for the approach and the Lion Rock Pass alternative. Rappel counts and rope length left out (one source).

set.approach: From the end of the logging road, follow the well-cairned trail to the Church Domes. Take the normal approach toward the south face of the Rectory, then bushwhack second class up and right past the Rectory's east face then traverse east across to the base of the Mosque, going by the Convent and the Valley of Death. The route is the most obvious crack on the south face prow of the Mosque, which opens with a tricky wide crack trending up and left.
set.descent_text: Rappel the neighbouring Kaddish route on the west face of the Mosque. You have to rappel hard south to find the second anchor, which is semi-hanging, and the line drops toward the Valley of Death.

review.notes: Approach from the Church Domes and Mosque area pages; descent from the route page. Rappel count and rope left out (one source).

set.approach: Aim for the north shore of Roosevelt Lake, beneath the North Ridge of Mt Conness. Parties get there from Tuolumne Meadows via Young Lakes and some cross-country travel, from Saddlebag Lake over the notch in the Conness North Ridge and down fourth-class slabs on its west side, or up the fourth-class chute used for the Conness West Ridge from Sawmill Campground. The Middle Buttress is the obvious one to start with. Scramble fourth and low fifth class ledges and pine bushes to a crack line directly below the large white right-facing corner in the centre of the buttress, and start in the small alcove above the last pine brush.
set.descent_text: From the top, move down and right off the sandy ledge and take a third-class gully to the summit plateau. Then cross the plateau to the steep chute just left of the northernmost buttress to reach the north end of Roosevelt Lake, or walk the easy ground south to reach the south end of the lake and the meadows.

review.notes: Area page for the approach; route page for the start position and any stated descent.

set.approach: Aim for the north shore of Roosevelt Lake, beneath the North Ridge of Mt Conness. Parties get there from Tuolumne Meadows via Young Lakes and some cross-country travel, from Saddlebag Lake over the notch in the Conness North Ridge and down fourth-class slabs on its west side, or up the fourth-class chute used for the Conness West Ridge from Sawmill Campground. The route starts at the bottom right end of the Middle Buttress, below a bulge of stacked blocks that looks like an arete, and works up natural weaknesses to the lower right point of the arete.
set.descent_text: Finish by moving down onto the sandy ledges on the far side of the summit block, then descend sandy slopes to the north or south end of Roosevelt Lake.

review.notes: Area page for the approach; route page for the start position and any stated descent.

set.approach: Leave the car at the pack station where the Pine Creek road ends and follow the Pine Creek Pass Trail until the Brownstone Mine crag appears just off the trail on the left. Miner Wall sits below and to the left of the main buttress, easy to see from the trail, with a little more talus hopping needed. The route is the clear crack that runs up the centre of the wall.
set.descent_text: From the bolted first-pitch anchor, lower; stepping right reaches the lower-off anchor of the neighbouring route. A second pitch ends at a tree anchor.

review.notes: Area page for the approach; route page for the start position and any stated descent.
